versions.changelog:
implementing-architecture 1.0.2

- Clarified usage for brownfield scenarios: this skill now explicitly applies when refactoring existing prototypes/codebases to conform to an approved architecture (not just greenfield implementation).
- Added "Brownfield rule": made clear that existing code is not architectural authority; implementation means bringing code into compliance, not treating prototypes as source of truth.
- Expanded "When NOT to Use" with rules for handling prototypes and what to do if architecture changes are needed.
- No behavioral or technical changes—documentation/business process clarification only.

implementing-architecture 1.0.1

- Added a homepage field and extended metadata to improve discoverability and integration.
- No changes to workflow, instructions, or file structure.
- No user-facing logic or functionality changes.

Initial release of implementing-architecture skill.

- Introduces a workflow for implementing code based on an approved architecture in docs/architecture/.
- Provides detailed guidance on when and when not to use this skill, emphasizing the need for STATUS: APPROVED in architecture.yaml.
- Explains the contract of the repo structure and roles of key files and directories.
- Outlines strict read-only handling for architecture artifacts and instructions for resolving discrepancies.
- Details a step-by-step implementation workflow including a mandatory preflight verification and capability checks before any code is written.
